response.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT i.InvoiceId, c.Country, AVG(il.UnitPrice) AS avg_price FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId GROUP BY i.InvoiceId, c.Country), dev AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, avg_price - (SELECT AVG(avg_price) FROM inv) AS deviation FROM inv), cd AS (SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, deviation, deviation - AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY Country) AS dev_minus_country FROM dev), r AS (SELECT cd.*, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY CASE WHEN dev_minus_country IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, dev_minus_country DESC) AS rnk FROM cd) SELECT InvoiceId, Country, avg_price, deviation, dev_minus_country FROM r WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY rnk, InvoiceId

assumptions.assumption: Country is the customer's country (Customer.Country), as the request says, not Invoice.BillingCountry.
An invoice's average unit price is a plain AVG of InvoiceLine.UnitPrice across its lines, not weighted by Quantity.
Invoices with no lines are kept, via a LEFT JOIN. Their average is NULL, so they are ignored in the overall and country averages and sort last.
Customers with a NULL country form one group for the country average.
